rules.message: Container runs privileged. A privileged container has effectively full access to the host. Drop privileged and grant only the specific capabilities the workload needs.

rules.messageTemplate: Pod shares a host namespace ({path} = {after}). This removes the isolation boundary between the pod and the node. Confirm the workload genuinely needs host-level access.

rules.message: runAsNonRoot was disabled or dropped, so the container may run as UID 0. Set runAsNonRoot: true and give the image a non-root user.
allowPrivilegeEscalation was enabled or its explicit false was removed. A process can then gain more privileges than its parent (setuid binaries, file capabilities). Pin it back to false.

rules.messageTemplate: Container adds the {after} Linux capability, which is close to full host privilege. Add only the narrow capability the workload needs, or drop the change.
Container image "{after}" is not pinned: it resolves to :latest, so what actually runs can change without a manifest change. Pin an immutable tag or a @sha256 digest.
imagePullPolicy moved from {before} to Always, so a restart can silently pull different bits behind the same tag. Keep IfNotPresent with a pinned tag or digest.
Replica count jumped from {before} to {after} (>=3x). Confirm the cluster has the capacity and that the cost is intended.
Resource limit {path} was removed. An unbounded container can starve everything else scheduled on the node.
Service type is {after}, which exposes the workload outside the cluster (a public load balancer, or a port open on every node). Confirm the exposure is intended and covered by network policy.
